Barista

Class-level protocols from documentation alone

3

Typestate specifications catch these violations at compile time

SocketRefinements.java
@StateSet({"unconnected", "bound", "connected", …}) @StateRefinement(to="unconnected(this)") void Socket(); @StateRefinement(from="unconnected(this)", to="bound(this)") void bind(SocketAddress b); @StateRefinement(from="bound(this)", to="connected(this)") void connect(SocketAddress e); @StateRefinement(from="connected(this)") InputStream getInputStream();
The implicit protocol, made explicit
s = new Socket();
s.bind(addr);
s.getInputStream();
State Refinement Error, line 3found bound(s) but expected connected(s)

Can LLM agents turn the protocol described in documentation into a machine-verifiable specification?

Barista turns documentation into verified LiquidJava specifications

Barista workflow · Step 1

Step 1: the agent extracts the protocol as a DFA

in Javadoc as JSON
out Mermaid state machine
MCP validation, until all pass
Every public method appears Every state is reachable Transitions are deterministic
7

Barista workflow · Steps 2–3

Steps 2–3: the DFA drives both tests and refinements

2 · Synthesize tests

DFA paths become test templates; the agent fills the [?] until they compile

@Test valid
s = new Socket([InetAddress a], [int port]);
s.close();
@Test invalid
s = new Socket();
s.sendUrgentData([int data]);
3 · Synthesize refinements

States and transitions map mechanically; the agent adds argument constraints

from DFA · MCP
@StateRefinement(from="bound(this)",
                 to="connected(this)")
from docs · agent
Socket(InetAddress a,
  @Refinement("ValidPort(_)") int port)
8

Barista workflow · Step 4

Step 4: LiquidJava checks the spec against the tests

SocketRefinements.java · annotated class
@StateRefinement(from="bound(this)",
                 to="connected(this)")
void connect(SocketAddress e);
@StateRefinement(from="connected(this)")
InputStream getInputStream();
@Test valid
s.bind(addr);
s.connect(addr);
s.getInputStream();
@Test invalid
s.bind(addr);
// no connect
s.getInputStream();
→
verifier via MCP
→
valid test passes
invalid test is rejectedfound bound(s) but expected connected(s)
Any mismatch returns the error message to the agent, which refines the spec until every test is classified correctly or it reaches max iterations

Takeaways and next steps

  1. 1

    Documentation is enough to bootstrap typestate specs

    High precision; a starting point for experts, not a replacement

  2. 2

    Intermediate representation for precision, tests for recall

    The gains come from the pipeline, more than from multi-agent orchestration. They help developers understand object protocols.

  3. 3

    Next: richer representations than the DFA

    Symbolic automata or extended FSMs for parameter-conditional transitions
